chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Nasr ibn Sa'id, the freedman of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The publiciser of the secret is a doubter, and its speaker in the presence of those other than its deserving ones is a disbeliever; and whoever holds fast to the Firmest Handle, he will be saved.' I said, 'And what is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The submission (to God's will/peace).'

key_terms.الْعُرْوَةُ الْوُثْقَى: The Firmest Handle (a Quranic term for the strongest bond with God)
key_terms.شَاكٌّ: A doubter (one who is uncertain in faith)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of someone who publicly reveals a secret according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual peril of revealing secrets to the concept of *shakk* (doubt or uncertainty), suggesting that indiscretion reflects an unstable faith. The hadith culminates in a profound theological definition, identifying *al-taslim* (complete submission to God's will) as the 'Firmest Handle' (*al-'urwah al-wuthqa*), thereby connecting the practical ethic of discretion with the core Shia principle of total reliance on the Divine. This interpretation emphasizes that true salvation is secured not merely by ritual, but by the internal state of surrendering one's will to God.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Nasr Bin Saaid, a slave of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his father who said, ‘

I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A publiciser of the secrets is a doubter, and its speaker in the presences of other than its deserving ones is a disbeliever; and the one who attaches with the Firmest Handle, so he would be saved’. I said, ‘And what is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The submission’.
en.sarwar: 10. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Nasr ibn Sa’id, Mawla abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) from his father who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The propagator (of the confidential Hadith of ‘ A’immah ) is in doubt (about his belief in ‘ A’immah ) and the narrator (of confidential matter) before a stranger (unreliable audience) is an unbeliever. Whoever holds fast to the firm ring, is saved.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is it (the ring)?’ The Imam said, ‘It is submission (to the commands of ‘ A’immah , and acceptance of the same).”’
